title: The first 7" ever pressed
body: Before albums existed, the small 7-inch record at 45 rpm was how most people heard new songs — one track per side, usually under three minutes. Many of our mixes still borrow that A-side / B-side structure.

title: How Night Bus got its cover
body: The artwork for 'Night Bus Frequencies' started as a photo of a fogged-up window; the halftone pattern you see is literally the grain of that photo pushed to the limit in a scanner.

title: Why risograph prints look like that
body: Risographs print one fluorescent ink at a time, so colors overlap imperfectly. That slight misregistration — the fuzzy edges and unexpected blends — is exactly what we try to imitate digitally in 'Paper Grooves'.
